a0.source: new: Pelland et al. (OSF 6z3xu) multilevel fit, untrained weekly strength gain at saturating volume; some/experienced: OpenPowerlifting within-person curves (careers ≥8 y), headroom ÷ time constant

headroom_median.source: OpenPowerlifting within-person curves: some = headroom from first meet, experienced = headroom left 3 years later; new = some ÷ (1+δ), δ = trained vs untrained rate (Pelland fit)

log_headroom_sd.source: OpenPowerlifting: sd of log individual headroom, careers ≥3 y with ≥5 meets

k_median.source: Pelland et al. multilevel strength fit: weekly fractional sets where returns flatten

log_k_sd.source: Pelland fit, study-bootstrap sd of log k (population uncertainty; individual variation in k is not identifiable from aggregate trials)

log_rho_sd.source: Steele et al. 2023 data (CC-BY 4.0): individual-response SD in RCT strength outcomes relative to mean change

sigma_median.source: Grgic et al. 2020: median 1RM test-retest CV 4.2% (32 studies, n=1595)

log_sigma_sd.source: Grgic et al. 2020 CV range 0.5–12.1% treated as ±2 sd on the log scale

process_sd.source: OpenPowerlifting: weekly drift from consecutive-meet residual changes vs gap, pooled across sexes

report_bias.source: Halperin et al. meta-analysis: reps to failure under-predicted by 0.95 (12 studies, n=414)

strength_slope_per_rir.source: Robinson et al. 2024 (OSF 7knsj) multilevel fit: strength gain vs estimated RIR

hypertrophy_slope_per_rir.source: Robinson et al. 2024 multilevel fit: hypertrophy gain vs estimated RIR

missing_rir.source: Robinson et al. 2024: median estimated RIR across strength-trial groups

strength_sets_90pct.source: Pelland fit: weekly fractional sets reaching 90% of the maximal volume-driven strength gain

hypertrophy_median_studied.source: Pelland data: median weekly sets (indirect weighted by w) in hypertrophy groups (no plateau identifiable up to 45)

strength_session_ceiling.source: Pelland et al. data, fit_session.py: sets per session where the strength stimulus saturates (dose = Σ sessions c·(1 − e^(−sets/c))). Likely reflects practice of the tested lift as well as physiology.

hypertrophy_session_ceiling.source: fit_session.py: no per-session ceiling for hypertrophy; ceilings under ~12 sets per session were rejected.

indirect_set_weight.source: Pelland et al. data, fit_indirect.py: how much a set counts for a muscle it trains indirectly (direct = 1). The 0.5 convention lies inside the interval; the data cannot separate the two.

volume.hypertrophy_curve_note: Hypertrophy rose roughly linearly across 0–45 weekly sets in the within- and between-study fit; k was not identifiable.

minutes_per_set.source: Pelland data: median inter-set rest 2.0 min (IQR 1.5–2.0, 572 groups) + ~30 s for a 10-rep set (median reps 10; ~3 s/rep assumed)

starting_strength.source: Pelland et al. (OSF 6z3xu) and Steele et al. 2023 pre-training 1RMs; log(1RM/body mass) regression; sex gap and deadlift/squat ratio from OpenPowerlifting
starting_strength.model: log(1RM/body mass) = intercept[exercise] + sex_gap[region]·male + trained·[experience ≠ new] + age_per_decade·(age−25)/10

decisions: Starting loads by analogy (e.g. incline bench from flat bench) add 0.25 to the log-scale 1σ; penalty arbitrary.
Experience "1–3 years" and "3+ years" both use the trial "trained" strength level; no data separates them.

Default weekly sets per muscle: strength and general goals use the volume reaching 90% of the fitted strength curve (one more set adds <10% of the first set’s gain); the muscle goal uses the median studied hypertrophy volume because no plateau is identifiable.
Experience mapping for OpenPowerlifting: "1–3 years" ≈ first competition, "3+ years" ≈ three years of competing later.
Novice headroom assumes the same approach time constant as trained lifters, scaled by the trial-measured untrained/trained rate ratio.
Strength effort weighting is flat: the Robinson strength slope is indistinguishable from zero.
Sport muscle priorities for coaches, not fitted.
